product_guards: Shared titles or descriptions are a detection heuristic, not proof of duplicate content. Require coherent direct HTML 200 observations, no noindex, matching content sketch, word count, H1, language, images and links; ambiguous metadata bridges and incomplete groups are refused.
Prefer a unique observed self-canonical master, otherwise use the stable shortest-URL convention. Preserve the existing mandatory human review and draft-PR workflow even for model-free corrections.

Bind all missing-canonical pages and any existing master to unique, non-shared literal HTML source files. Before any PUT, verify current canonicals, complete budget, readable blob SHAs, matching literal bodies and languages, and bounded patch format.

Refuse current noindex, base elements, scripts, templates, malformed head structure, duplicated attributes and ambiguous content lookalikes. Add only one canonical and align only an already-present literal og:url. Preserve other metadata, alternates, navigation, bodies and line endings.

Do not call a provider or AI file picker, and do not bill tokens. URL and GitHub free-form previews and confirmation cannot bypass these checks through cached previews; individual deep correction and bulk correction share the bounded implementation.

The preflight prevents known incomplete plans, not all partial remote writes: GitHub per-file PUTs are not atomic. Stop on write failure and leave any partial draft for review; never auto-merge this convention.
Keep the auditor, catalog and historical receipts unchanged. Metadata-only negative witnesses stay detectable and are explicitly listed as refused.

limitations: This is an owned static-HTML acceptance test, not every stack or customer site. Scripts, structured data, computed templates, ambiguous routes and insufficient observations are conservatively refused. Metadata-only witnesses remain anomalies; refusal is not a repair.

Native previews remain noindex, so their duplicate-family counts are 0 before and after. The existing exact preview-host/header projection with saved sitemap measures indexable scoring, not production indexation. Served canonicals independently prove the HTML change.

The final ambiguous-content-attribute guard was added after the live cycle. A fresh read-only countercheck against the final code revalidated the exact baseline and builds; both positive HTML patches are unchanged and covered by the final tests.

The consolidated secondary URL still needs sitemap cleanup. Human review of the canonical convention is mandatory; per-file network failures are not atomic. No global all-green or client-readiness verdict is claimed.

No production recovery replay, receipt migration, agent deployment, onboarding, scheduler, payment workflow, capacity test or fresh PostgreSQL run is included. The SQLite suite retains its existing skipped tests.
